parole.significato: A traveller or merchant from the Middle East
parole.testo: From Arabic خَوَاجَا (ḵawājā, “gentleman”), from Classical Persian خواجه (xwāja, “gentleman”). The term came to be applied to merchants because they were formerly the chief travellers. Doublet of hodja.

parole.significato: A large, vaulted chamber with a monumental arched opening on one side.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِيوَان (ʔīwān), from Classical Persian اَیْوَان (aywān, “porch”); see there for more. Doublet of apadana.

parole.significato: A hostel for Sufis, often in the form of cells around a courtyard.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic خَانَقَاه (ḵānaqāh), from Classical Persian خَانَگَاه (xānagāh), from خَانَه (xāna, “house”) + ـگَاه (-gāh).

parole.significato: A kind of dagger used in certain Arabian countries.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic خَنْجَر (ḵanjar). Doublet of kindjal.

parole.significato: A member of a particular fundamentalist Sufi order.
parole.testo: From Arabic الْقَادِرِيَّة (al-qādiriyya) and/or Classical Persian قادریه (qādiriyya), named after Abdul Qadir Gilani.

parole.significato: A board game, an ancestor of modern chess.
parole.testo: From Arabic شَطْرَنْج (šaṭranj), from Early Classical Persian چَتْرَنْگ (čatrang), from Middle Persian 𐭰𐭠𐭲𐭫𐭠𐭭𐭢 (ctlng /⁠čatrang⁠/), from Sanskrit चतुरङ्ग (caturaṅga).

parole.significato: A tall brimless hat, usually conical or curved on top, worn in Muslim countries as a sign of distinction and prestige.
parole.testo: Arabic تَاج (tāj) from Classical Persian تاج (tāj, “crown”). Doublet of tag.
